_meta.indication: VYVGART is a neonatal Fc receptor blocker indicated for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter (56 study centers), multinational (15 countries), randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled phase 3 study; subjects received 4-week treatment cycles of once-weekly infusions of efgartigimod 10 mg/kg or placebo on stable background therapy
pivotal_trials.population: Adults with generalized myasthenia gravis on stable background therapy; enrolled AChR-Ab seropositive (77%) and seronegative (23%) subjects, with the primary endpoint evaluated in the AChR-Ab seropositive population
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Percentage of AChR-Ab seropositive subjects who, after the first treatment cycle, had a decrease of at least 2 points on the total MG-ADL for at least 4 consecutive weeks (MG-ADL responders)
pivotal_trials.result: In the AChR-Ab seropositive population, MG-ADL responders were 67.7% with efgartigimod vs 29.7% with placebo (odds ratio 4.95, p<0.0001)

nct_ctgov.title: An Efficacy and Safety Study of ARGX-113 in Patients With Myasthenia Gravis Who Have Generalized Muscle Weakness

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=10%) are respiratory tract infections, headache, and urinary tract infection. In Study 1704, respiratory tract infection occurred in 33% (efgartigimod) vs 29% (placebo), headache 32% vs 29%, urinary tract infection 10% vs 5%, and myalgia 6% vs 1%; infections were AEs of special interest and five deaths were reported in the long-term extension Study 1705
target_moa: Efgartigimod is a human IgG1 antibody fragment engineered to bind the neonatal Fc receptor (FcRn); by blocking FcRn it inhibits FcRn-mediated recycling of IgG, shortening IgG half-life and reducing circulating IgG including pathogenic autoantibodies
modality: other (human IgG1-derived Fc fragment / antibody fragment)

advisory_committee.vote: Advisory Committee Summary: Not applicable (no advisory committee convened)

description.text: Updated vaccination language in Dosage and Administration and Infections warning sections (labeling change, not a new indication)

citations.quote: These prior approval sBLAs provide for changes to language regarding vaccination in the Dosage and Administration section (2.1 Recommended Vaccination) and in the Warnings and Precautions section (5.1 Infections) of the Prescribing Information.

description.text: Revised dosing to remove statement that safety of initiating subsequent cycles sooner than 50 days was not established, and added subsequent-cycle safety information

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sBLAs provide for revisions to the Prescribing Information in the Dosage and Administration section (subsection 2.2) to remove the statement about safety of initiating subsequent cycles sooner than 50 days not being established and in the Adverse Reactions section (subsection 6.1) to provide safety information regarding subsequent cycles.

description.text: Expanded gMG indication to include adult patients who are AChR-Ab seronegative, removing the prior AChR antibody positive qualifier

citations.quote: These Prior Approval sBLAs provide for expansion of the indication to include the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor antibody (AChR-Ab) seronegative. Therefore, the indication has been revised to remove the prior qualifier of adult patients who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive to expand the indication to the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) in adult patients.

basis.text: A preliminary breakthrough therapy designation request advice was discussed but FDA determined it was premature since the sponsor had not submitted data demonstrating improvement over available therapies

citations.quote: On April 11, 2018, the Sponsor submitted a preliminary breakthrough therapy designation request advice form. As discussed in a teleconference held on May 31, 2018, it was determined that it was premature to discuss a breakthrough therapy designation request since the Sponsor did not submit data demonstrating an improvement over available therapies for the treatment of MG.

basis.text: Fast track designation was granted on February 18, 2020, based on the potential to address an unmet medical need, specifically to treat patients seronegative for AChR antibodies

citations.quote: Fast track designation was granted on February 18, 2020. Although there are two approved therapies for MG (pyridostigmine bromide and eculizumab), efgartigimod had potential to address an unmet medical need specifically to treat patients who are seronegative for acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibodies.

orphan_indication.text: Efgartigimod was granted orphan drug designation on September 20, 2017 for the treatment of myasthenia gravis; the sponsor was exempted from PREA requirements

Because efgartigimod for the treatment of generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) was granted orphan designation, the Applicant was exempted from the Pediatric Research Equity Act requirements.

basis.text: The applicant requested priority review, but the Division determined the application did not appear to provide data addressing an unmet need in gMG and granted a standard review

citations.quote: The Applicant requested priority review in their BLA submission on December 17, 2020. The Division determined that the application did not appear to provide data to address an unmet need in gMG and granted a standard review.

summary.text: BLA 761195 was submitted 12/17/2020 and received a standard (not priority) review after FDA denied the applicant's priority review request; efgartigimod had orphan drug designation (granted September 20, 2017) and fast track designation (granted February 18, 2020), but breakthrough therapy designation was not pursued and it was not an accelerated approval; approval was based on the pivotal Study 1704.

citations.quote: Argenx BV submitted a biologics license application (BLA) 761195 for efgartigimod. Efgartigimod is a first-in-class, neonatal Fc receptor blocker for the treatment of adults with generalized myasthenia gravis (gMG) who are anti-acetylcholine receptor (AChR) antibody positive.

The Applicant requested priority review in their BLA submission on December 17, 2020. The Division determined that the application did not appear to provide data to address an unmet need in gMG and granted a standard review.
Fast track designation was granted on February 18, 2020.
Not applicable. Efgartigimod was granted orphan drug designation. Pediatric assessments are waived.

requirement.text: PMR 4202-1: Conduct a worldwide descriptive pregnancy/lactation study collecting prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Vyvgart to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications and adverse effects on the fetus, neonate, and infant (infant outcomes assessed through at least the first year of life)

citations.quote: 4202-1 Conduct a worldwide descriptive study that collects prospective and retrospective data in women exposed to Vyvgart (efgartigimod) during pregnancy and/or lactation to assess risk of pregnancy and maternal complications, adverse effects on the developing fetus and neonate, and adverse effects on the infant. Infant outcomes will be assessed through at least the first year of life. The minimum number of patients will be specified in the protocol.
